sections.content: How many people are "electricians and electrical fitters"?

190,455 people

were counted on the census as "electricians and electrical fitters" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Electricians and electrical fitters assemble parts in the manufacture of electrical and electronic equipment, and install, maintain, and repair electrical plant, machinery, appliances and wiring.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "electricians and electrical fitters" there were more men than women (98.4% compared with 1.6%).

This means "electricians and electrical fitters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 98.4% and women made up 1.6% of "electricians and electrical fitters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "electricians and electrical fitters" included:

  • plumbers and heating and ventilating installers and repairers
  • glaziers, window fabricators and fitters
  • floorers and wall tilers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "electricians and electrical fitters", 13.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "electricians and electrical fitters" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "electricians and electrical fitters" included:

  • delivery operatives
  • vehicle technicians, mechanics and electricians
  • collector salespersons and credit agents

We can look at who worked as "electricians and electrical fitters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "electricians and electrical fitters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "electricians and electrical fitters", 6.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (89.2% compared with 10.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (58.2%) than self-employed (41.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
